title: Random Pick Index
statement:
Write a class `Solution` around an integer array `nums`, which may contain repeated values:

- `Solution(nums)` stores the array.
- `pick(target)` returns an index `i` with `nums[i] == target`. When `target` occurs at several indices, each of them must be returned with the same probability. `target` always occurs in `nums`.

Use `Math.random()` for randomness; it is seeded here, so every run is repeatable. Because answers are random, the judge accepts any matching index, and when a case picks the same target many times it also checks that the matching indices come up about equally often.
constraints: target is a value that occurs in nums.
At most 10^4 calls are made to pick.
notes:
## Intuition

The direct way stores, for every value, the list of its indices, and `pick` returns a random entry of that list: O(1) per pick but O(n) extra memory. **Reservoir sampling** needs no extra memory: scan `nums` once, and when the `count`-th match appears, make it the current choice with probability `1/count`. A match seen at position `m` among `k` matches is chosen with probability `1/m` and then survives every later match, so it ends up chosen with probability `1/m · m/(m+1) · … · (k-1)/k = 1/k`, the same for every match.

## Approach

1. Store `nums` in the constructor.
2. In `pick(target)`, set `chosen = -1` and `count = 0`.
3. Scan every index `i`. Skip values other than `target`.
4. For a match, increase `count`, then draw a random integer in `0..count-1`; if it is `0` (probability `1/count`), set `chosen = i`.
5. After the scan, return `chosen`. The first match is always taken (`count = 1`), so `chosen` is a real index.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1,2,3,3,3]`. For `pick(3)`, index 2 is the first match: `count = 1`, so `chosen = 2`. At index 3, `count = 2`: with probability 1/2 `chosen` becomes 3. At index 4, `count = 3`: with probability 1/3 `chosen` becomes 4. If that last draw hits, the answer is `4`, as in LeetCode's sample. `pick(1)` has a single match, so it always returns `0`. The next `pick(3)` might keep index 2 through both later draws and return `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) per `pick`, one scan of `nums`.
- Space: O(1) beyond the stored array.

## Pitfalls

- Replace with probability `1/count`, where `count` counts matches only, not all indices scanned so far.
- Do not stop at the first match or return early: later matches must get their chance.
- Draw a new random number for every match; reusing one draw for the whole scan breaks the probabilities.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nums` | the stored array |
| `count` | how many indices holding `target` the scan has met so far |
| `chosen` | the index currently kept in the reservoir |
| `i` | the index being scanned |

narration.3: Keep the array; each pick scans it again.
narration.7: No match has been kept yet.
narration.8: Count the matches seen during this scan.
narration.10: Only indices holding target take part in the draw.
narration.11: One more match has been seen.
narration.12: Draw a number in 0..count-1; zero happens with probability 1/count.
narration.13: Keep this index, replacing the earlier choice.
narration.17: Every match had an equal 1/count chance in the end; return the kept index.
